thread:
incident-bot: RED ALERT: GPU queue length > 9,000 in us-west-2. Autoscaler attempted scale but hit node_max=120 and failed to provision. Throttling observed on user-facing queue. Pager triggered at 21:08 UTC.

alice: seeing large backlog on /generate, a lot of long-context jobs. latency spikes to >10s and 503s for some customers. I’m taking this.

raj: oncall-ack. can you paste the autoscaler log?

alice: logs: 
```
2026-03-15T21:07:58Z autoscaler: desired=160 current=120 max_nodes=120 -> scale_blocked(max_reached)
2026-03-15T21:08:02Z scheduler: queue_len=9123 pending_pods=320 unschedulable
```

maria: fwiw we deployed a new batch-priority flag last release; could be bumping resource reqs. tagging infra.

opsbot: @infra please note manual-cap-raise request pending. SLA impact: potential 5-15% error increase for high-throughput customers.

alice: initial mitigation: 1) flip low-priority queue to deferred, 2) enable model-fallback route to small-quantized variants, 3) open manual node cap request. Doing 1 & 2 now.

jordan: +1 on fallback route. doing a quick config push to route traffic for tier=free to quantized-small.

alice: applied: 
- pushed routing rule -> free -> model-x-small-q
- paused batch ingestion from external feeder for 10m
Result: queue dropped to ~6k but still slow drain.

raj: manual cap raise needed. infra has policy: manual bumps require ops lead + oncall signoff. pinging @raj-ops-lead for approval.

alice: tagging @raj for approval (oncall). Estimated new max_nodes=180 to clear backlog in ~12-18m.

support-bot: Customer impact: 3 paying tenants showing 504/503 errors intermittently (IDs: TEN-344, TEN-998, TEN-121). Notified support to open tickets and apply temporary credits.

raj: I approve manual bump to 180 for emergency. leaving note: must revert to 120 after drain.

maria: ops lead (sam) verbally approved on call. opsbot: approval recorded by sam at 21:15 UTC.

alice: initiating cap bump request to infra runbook. Command used (internal):
```
# request to capacity ops
POST /internal/infra/cap-bump
payload: { region: "us-west-2", new_max_nodes: 180, reason: "autoscale hit ceiling - emergency bump" }
```

opsbot: infra: received manual-cap-bump requestid=cap-20260315-021. Provisioning additional nodes (spot + reserved mix). ETA ~5-8m.

jordan: monitoring cluster: new instances starting; kube-scheduler showing 45 new pods pending->running.

alice: queue drain rate improving. current queue: 3400. p50 latency back to ~220ms for routed requests.

support-bot: updated customer tickets with ETA for mitigation and credit plans. Public status incident page: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1912345678 (ops: keep updated).

raj: note - root cause suspicion: recent change increased GPU memory requests for certain model configs. please open a postmortem ticket and assign to eng-ml.

maria: creating eval task to repro with longer sequences and new batch-priority flag. will attach perf traces.

opsbot: manual bump completed at 21:24 UTC. new max_nodes=180 applied.

alice: all green: backlog drained. final queue 0 for high-priority routes, low-priority still draining with no customer impact.

jordan: verifying autoscaler metrics; it will not shrink below baseline for 30m to avoid oscillation.

alice: full mitigation done. next steps: 1) rollback batch-priority resource bump or tune it, 2) postmortem, 3) update runbook to include faster approval path for emergency cap bumps.

raj: agreed. thanks all. I’ll file incident and assign owners.

maria: postmortem ticket created: PM-INC-1912345678 with assignees @eng-ml, @eng-sre.

alice: closing thread. marking incident resolved at 21:41 UTC. :white_check_mark:
